commits.headline: fix(item-randomizer): keep the Items-menu checks in the mod's one save record
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body: A mod has one save record: save_data_set replaces it. #202's Items-menu runtime wrote its own record (MIT1) while the gold-case and NPC checks of #196 and #199 write theirs (RFR1), so each write discarded the other's checks. The item randomizer now keeps the six Items-menu checks and the consumed Raritanium in bits 23 to 29 of the gold-case and NPC record, only for this seed's game. Archipelago, which keeps its other checks in the save itself, still uses the runtime's own record.

commits.headline: feat(ng-plus-plus): bolt rules for challenge mode runs, with their tests
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The pure rules behind platinum bolts and bolt scaling, apart from the
game: the run scale from challenge mode's second run (cycle 2) in step
with the tiers' price factors (x1.5, x2.5, x4, x6; generous x1.5 more),
an enemy's toughness from its own bolts (x1 up to 20, the square root
of its bolts over 20 past it, at most x2), the platinum share by run
and kill streak (10% to 50% in cycle 2 up to 25% to 90% from cycle 5),
the scaled amount, and the split of a drop into platinum coins (worth
five…

commits.headline: feat(ng-plus-plus): platinum bolts and bolt scaling on OpenRAC's bolt hook points
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
From challenge mode's second run, rac2.bolt.spawn_pickups runs the
game's burst with its amount times the run scale and the enemy's
toughness (its own bolts at +0xB4 when its class record says enemy),
so the game's roll, doubling, pacing and coin limit still decide the
total. The coins it makes through rac2.bolt.spawn_pickup are only
written down; their total is then made again as platinum and gold
coins at the places and speeds the game chose (on the game's stack),
the platinum ones drawn with…

commits.headline: docs(ng-plus-plus): platinum bolts and bolt scaling in plain words, 0.3.0
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The README's new section: the platinum bolt set (5 to 5,000), the
bolts per new game (x1.5, x2.5, x4, x6; generous x2.25 to x9), tough
enemies up to x2, the platinum share by kill streak (10% to 90%), the
setting, and what an OpenRAC before interface 1.23 does. How it works,
the files and the tests name the bolt hook points and the new parts.
The manifest's and listing's descriptions and the repository's mod
table mention the bolts; the version is 0.3.0.

commits.headline: fix(ng-plus-plus): take the bolt collect hook as void(u32), 0.3.1
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The port's rac2.bolt.collect is void(u32); asking for u32(u32) made the
port refuse the hook and leave the whole mod unloaded.

commits.headline: List gc-magneboots (#234)
commits.author: Promises
commits.body:
* List gc-magneboots

Going Commando Magneboots (https://github.com/Promises/rac1-gc-magneboots):
Going Commando's Gravity Boots in place of the Magneboots. Needs mod
interface 1.23 (the hook points of OpenRAC #590).

commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
5% of a drop at x1 up to 25% at x20, the drops themselves unscaled; the
run scale and toughness still start at the second challenge mode.

commits.headline: fix(ng-plus-plus): leave the bolt hook points out of the manifest until a released SDK knows them, 0.3.3
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
package_mod from SDK 1.20.0 rejects rac2.bolt.* as unknown hook points,
so the 0.3.1 and 0.3.2 tag builds packaged nothing. The port only warns
about an unlisted hook point.

commits.headline: fix(ng-plus-plus): more platinum in the first challenge mode, log the first drops, 0.3.4
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
At 5% a drop under 100 bolts paid no platinum at all; 20% at x1 up to
40% at x20 shows one from 25 bolts. The first five drops of a session
go to the log with their total, streak, scale and platinum coins.
